367140.title: Unimodality conjecture for Toda eigenfunction numerators
367140.statement:
For $\alpha\in Q^{\geq 0}$, let $\mathfrak{J}_\alpha$ be the Toda eigenfunction and let $(q)_\alpha$ be the associated $q$-factorial. A polynomial is **unimodal** if its coefficient sequence weakly increases to a maximum and then weakly decreases. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak{J}_\alpha
$$

is unimodal. This is motivated by empirical observations after the positivity conjecture; the source gives no proof or resolution.
367140.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10655

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
367140.source_name: Antoine Labelle, “On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions”, arXiv:2502.10655 (2026).

progress.label: Open
progress.tldr: The conjecture remains unproved: experiments support it, but the proposed geometric route depends on another unproved conjecture.
progress.summary:
A. Labelle formulates the conjecture for every nonnegative root-lattice element: the numerator $(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak{J}_\alpha$ should have coefficients that rise and then fall. The paper records empirical support but gives no general proof or resolution.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/2502.10655)*

**Known results**

- In type $A$, unimodality would follow from Labelle's Conjecture 6.1, which predicts a smooth projective variety with the relevant Poincare polynomial; this implication is conditional.
- Positivity in type $A$ is established by Labelle's Theorem 1.2, but positivity in general remains conjectural.


Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture is recorded and empirically supported, but no proof, verified counterexample, or resolution of general unimodality is reported.

*Caveats. No independent source corroborates a claimed counterexample or proof.*

solutions.body:
**Counterexample: the conjecture fails in every non-simply-laced irreducible Dynkin type.**

The exact current statement is Conjecture 7.3 of [A. Labelle, arXiv:2502.10655v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.10655), revised July 28, 2026. It asserts unimodality of
\[
P_\alpha(q)=(q)_\alpha^2\mathfrak J_\alpha(q)
\]
for every nonnegative root-lattice element of an arbitrary split semisimple root system.

Write
\[
d_i=\frac{(\alpha_i,\alpha_i)}2,
\qquad
D_a=\prod_i(q^{d_i};q^{d_i})_{a_i},
\qquad
Q(a)=\frac12\left(\sum_i a_i\alpha_i,\sum_i a_i\alpha_i\right).
\]
The source's defining recursion is
\[
(1-q^{Q(a)})\mathfrak J_a
=
\sum_{\substack{0\le b\le a\\b\ne a}}
\frac{q^{Q(b)}}{D_{a-b}}\mathfrak J_b,
\qquad
\mathfrak J_0=1.
\tag{1}
\]
Substituting \(P_b=D_b^2\mathfrak J_b\) gives the exact integral triangular recurrence
\[
(1-q^{Q(a)})P_a
=
\sum_{\substack{0\le b\le a\\b\ne a}}
q^{Q(b)}P_b
\prod_i
\left[
\binom{a_i}{b_i}_{q^{d_i}}
\prod_{j=b_i+1}^{a_i}(1-q^{d_i j})
\right].
\tag{2}
\]

Now take type \(B_2\), ordering the long root first. Then
\[
(d_1,d_2)=(2,1),
\qquad
\bigl((\alpha_i,\alpha_j)\bigr)
=
\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
Q(a,b)=2a^2-2ab+b^2.
\]
Applying (2) gives the complete small-index table
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
 &b=0&b=1&b=2\\ \hline
a=0&1&1&1\\
a=1&1&1+q+q^2&1+q+3q^2+q^3+q^4\\
a=2&1&1+q+q^2+q^3+q^4&
1+q+3q^2+2q^3+5q^4+2q^5+3q^6+q^7+q^8 .
\end{array}
\]
In particular, for \(\alpha=2\alpha_1+2\alpha_2\),
\[
\boxed{
P_\alpha(q)
=
1+q+3q^2+2q^3+5q^4+2q^5+3q^6+q^7+q^8.
}
\]
Every coefficient is strictly positive, and the polynomial is palindromic, but
\[
[q^2]P_\alpha=3>
[q^3]P_\alpha=2<
[q^4]P_\alpha=5.
\]
Hence \(P_\alpha\) is not unimodal.

The obstruction extends to every doubly-laced irreducible type. If a coefficient \(a_i=0\), every \(b\le a\) in (1) also has \(b_i=0\); thus the recursion depends only on the full Dynkin subdiagram supporting \(a\). Each \(B_r,C_r\) for \(r\ge2\), and \(F_4\), contains a \(B_2=C_2\) double-edge subdiagram. Put coefficient \(2\) on its two vertices and \(0\) elsewhere to obtain exactly the same nonunimodal polynomial.

For the remaining non-simply-laced type \(G_2\), take
\[
(d_1,d_2)=(1,3),
\qquad
Q(a,b)=a^2-3ab+3b^2,
\qquad
\alpha=3\alpha_1+3\alpha_2.
\]
The exact coefficient sequence from (2) is
\[
(1,2,5,11,16,24,39,46,60,84,88,99,119,110,
110,119,99,88,84,60,46,39,24,16,11,5,2,1).
\]
It again has positive full support and is palindromic, but contains
\[
119>110=110<119.
\]

Thus Conjecture 7.3 is false in every non-simply-laced irreducible Dynkin type. The separate simply-laced and type-\(A\) questions are not claimed here.

387833.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.96
387833.statement: For $-\infty<p<+\infty$ let \[B(p):=\sup\{\beta_f(p):f\text{ conformal map of }\mathbb{D}\text{ into }\mathbb{D}\}\] where \[\beta_f(p)=\limsup_{r\to1}\Big(\int_{|\zeta|=r}|f'(r\zeta)|^p\,|d\zeta|\Big)/\log\frac{1}{1-r}.\] The BCJK-conjecture states that \[ B(p)= \begin{cases} -p-1 & \text{for } p\leq-2, p^2/4 & \text{for } -2\leq p\leq2, p-1 & \text{for } p\geq2. \end{cases} \] The claim that $B(p)=|p|-1$ is the famous Brennan conjecture. Carleson and Jones proved that $B(p)=p-1+O((p-2)^2)$ as $p\to2$, $p>2$. Based on extensive computer experiments Kraetzer conjectured that $B(p)=p^2/4$ for $|p|\leq2$. See Garnett and Marshall . (Ch. Pommerenke)
387833.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

solutions.summary: Claimed by OpenAI. The manuscript claims a uniform inverse-first-power integral-means bound for normalized bounded univalent disk maps with logarithmic growth exponent strictly below one quarter, hence B_b(-1) < 1/4. This would contradict the stated quadratic spectrum with the standard logarithmic integral-means definition; the target’s displayed exponent omits the logarithm of the integral.

387859.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.6
387859.statement: We consider the range of the random function \[F(z)=\sum^\infty_{n=0}\pm a_nz^n\] ($F$ chosen at random in the natural way) defined in $\mathbb{D}$, where $\sum|a_n|^2=\infty$. Is the image of $w=F(z)$ with probability one [(a)] ; everywhere dense in the plane? ; the whole plane? ; does it contain any given point with probability one? If $a_n=n^\lambda$, $(b)$ holds if $\lambda>\frac{1}{2}$, and $(a)$ holds if $-\frac{1}{2}<\lambda<+\frac{1}{2}$. (J. P. Kahane)
387859.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

progress.label: Open
progress.tldr: A newer result settles analogous questions for complex random coefficients, but the original question about random signs has not been resolved.
progress.summary:
Kahane’s problem asks whether a random signed power series has an image that is almost surely dense in the plane, equal to the whole plane, or contains each prescribed point. Its stated power-law cases are known: density for $-\frac{1}{2}<\lambda<\frac{1}{2}$ and surjectivity for $\lambda>\frac{1}{2}$.

**Known results**

- For $a_n=n^\lambda$, the image is almost surely dense when $-\frac{1}{2}<\lambda<\frac{1}{2}$ (Kahane).
- For $a_n=n^\lambda$, the image is almost surely the whole plane when $\lambda>\frac{1}{2}$ (Kahane).

**Related random-analytic-function result**

A recent preprint proves almost-sure density for broad classes with rotationally invariant complex coefficients, and whole-plane coverage for unbounded critical-regular Gaussian series; it also states a whole-plane result when $\sum a_n^2=\infty$ in the rotationally invariant setting. These coefficients are not the independent signs $\pm a_n$ in Problem 7.6, so the exact problem remains unsettled.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.19380)*


Current status (as of August 2026): The quoted power-law cases are settled, but the general independent-sign problem in Problem 7.6 has no recorded direct resolution; only analogous complex-coefficient results are available.

*Caveats. The related preprint does not establish the claims for independent signs $\pm a_n$.*

367221.title: Coefficient relations in mixed Berndt-type integral formulas
367221.statement:
For each integer $m\ge 1$, let $c_{2,m}$, $e_{2,m}$, $d_{1,m}$, and $f_{1,m}$ be the numbers appearing in Theorems and. **Coefficient relations.** The following identities hold:

$$
c_{2,m}+e_{2,m}=0
$$

and

$$
d_{1,m}+f_{1,m}=0.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by comparing the coefficients in Examples and; its validity would reveal a systematic relation among the coefficients in the mixed Berndt-type integral formulas.
367221.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.15173

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
367221.source_name: Jianing Zhou, “Mixed Berndt-Type Integrals and Generalized Barnes Multiple Zeta Functions”, arXiv:2502.15173 (2026).

367032.title: The periodicity and unboundedness conjecture for shifted Hankel determinant sequences
367032.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\Delta_j^{(\ell)}$ denote the $j$th term of the Hankel determinant sequence shifted by $\ell$. Consider shifts with $\ell\geq n+2$.

**The case $\ell\geq n+2$.** The sequence $\Delta_j^{(n+2)}$ is $2n(n+1)$-periodic when $n$ is even and $2n(n+1)$-antiperiodic, hence $4n(n+1)$-periodic, when $n$ is odd, and its terms belong only to $\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}$, except when $n=1$, when they belong only to $\{-1,0,1\}$. All sequences $\Delta_j^{(\ell)}$ with $\ell\geq n+3$ are unbounded.

The statement extends the known periodicity results for shifts through $\ell=n+1$. It is proved for part (1) when $n=1$, while the general case remains open.
367032.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05993

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
367032.source_name: Guo-Niu Han and Emmanuel Pedon, “Hankel continued fractions and Hankel determinants for q-deformed metallic numbers”, arXiv:2502.05993 (2026).

366268.title: Logarithmic evaluation conjecture for a family of generalized continued fractions
366268.statement:
For an integer $k\geq 1$, consider the generalized continued fraction

$$
\mathcal{C}\left[\frac{n^2}{k^2(1-4n^2)}\right].
$$

**Logarithmic evaluation conjecture.** For all $k\geq 1$,

$$
\mathcal{C}\left[\frac{n^2}{k^2(1-4n^2)}\right]=\frac{2/k}{\operatorname{ln}(k+1)-\operatorname{ln}(k-1)}.
$$

These identities give explicit limits for a family of continued fractions that had previously been known to converge but whose limits were unknown. The supplied source reports that the formulas were verified numerically and describes them as conjectures; no proof or later resolution is given here.
366268.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.12361

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).
366268.source_name: Itay Beit-Halachmi and Ido Kaminer, “The Ramanujan Library – Automated Discovery on the Hypergraph of Integer Relations”, arXiv:2412.12361 (2025).

365749.title: Schoenberg's inequality for polynomial zeros and critical points
365749.statement:
Let $F$ be a complex polynomial of degree $n\geq 2$ with zeros $z_1,\dots,z_n$ and critical points $w_1,\dots,w_{n-1}$. **Schoenberg's conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|w_j|^2\leq \frac{1}{n^2}\left|\sum_{k=1}^n z_k\right|^2+\frac{n-2}{n}\sum_{k=1}^n|z_k|^2,
$$

with equality if and only if all $z_1,\dots,z_n$ are collinear in the complex plane. The conjecture was confirmed independently by Pereira and Malamud, and later reproved by Cheung--Ng and Kushel--Tyaglov.
365749.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.07105

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of November 2024). “Conjecture was confirmed independently by Pereira and Malamud .”
365749.source_name: Teng Zhang, “A refinement of Pawlowski's result”, arXiv:2411.07105 (2025).

365539.title: Louboutin's degree conjecture for the auxiliary Laurent polynomial
365539.statement:
Let $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ with $a\neq 0$ and $b\geq 1$, and let $m_{a,b}:=a^2+ab+b^2$. Using the polynomials and Laurent polynomials defined in Proposition 19, let $G_{a,b,m}(T)$ and $B_{a,b,m}$ be the associated quantities, with $M_{a,b}$ and $N_{a,b,m_{a,b}}$ taken from the cited table. **Louboutin's degree conjecture.** If $m_{a,b}$ is odd and at least $5$, and $(a,b)$ is not of the excluded forms $(-2b,b)$ with odd $b$, $(b,b)$ with odd $b$, or $(b,b)$ with even $b\geq 2$, then

$$
\deg G_{a,b,m_{a,b}}(T)<0\qquad\text{and}\qquad B_{a,b,m_{a,b}}\leq m_{a,b}.
$$

These inequalities assert the hypotheses needed in Proposition 19 and hence support the paper's main theorem; the supplied text does not specify whether the conjecture was already resolved.
365539.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.21158

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “This is still an open problem. Ennola conjectured in that $\{ \epsilon_l, \epsilon_l-1 \}$ above is a pair of fundamental units for the maximal order $\mathcal{O}$ of $\mathbb{Q}(\epsilon_l)$.”
365539.source_name: Jinwoo Choi and Dohyeong Kim, “On a weak form of Ennola's conjecture about certain cubic number fields”, arXiv:2410.21158 (2024).

365538.title: Louboutin's polynomial identity conjecture for S and R
365538.statement:
For $d\geq 1$, define

$$
P_d(X,Y)=d\sum_{\substack{k,l\geq 0\\0\leq 2k+3l\leq d}}(-1)^{k-1}\binom{k+l}{k}\binom{d-k-2l}{k+l}\frac{X^kY^{d-2k-3l}}{d-k-2l}.
$$

Let $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ be nonzero, put $c:=a+b\neq 0$, and define

$$
S_{a,b}(T)=T^{-a}+T^{-b}+T^{a+b}.
$$

For $d\in\{a,b,c\}$,

$$
P_{|d|}(S_{a,b}(T),S_{a,b}(1/T))=-S_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}).
$$

If $a$ is even and $b$ is odd, also define

$$
R_{a,b}(T)=T^{-a}-(-1)^{a+b}T^{-b}+T^{a+b}.
$$

Then

$$
P_{|d|}(-R_{a,b}(T),-R_{a,b}(1/T))=\begin{cases}-S_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}),&d=a,\\R_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}),&d\in\{b,c\}.\end{cases}
$$

This identity is one of Louboutin's conjectures used in the proof of the paper's main theorem; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.
365538.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.21158

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “This is still an open problem. Ennola conjectured in that $\{ \epsilon_l, \epsilon_l-1 \}$ above is a pair of fundamental units for the maximal order $\mathcal{O}$ of $\mathbb{Q}(\epsilon_l)$.”
365538.source_name: Jinwoo Choi and Dohyeong Kim, “On a weak form of Ennola's conjecture about certain cubic number fields”, arXiv:2410.21158 (2024).

365405.title: Proposed norm inequalities for extending the radius estimate to $1<p\leq2$
365405.statement:
Let $1<p<2$, set $r=2p/(2-p)$, and let $i_{p2}\colon\ell_p\to\ell_2$ be the formal identity map. Let $\pi_{r,2}(\cdot)$ denote the $(r,2)$-absolutely summing norm. For a linear map $B\colon\ell_2\to\ell_p$, let $\|B\|_{S_r}$ denote its $r$-Schatten norm,

$$
\|B\|_{S_r}=\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}(B^*B)^{r/2}\bigr)^{1/r}.
$$

For a positive semi-definite operator $A\colon\ell_{p'}\to\ell_p$, where $p'=p/(p-1)$, set $r=p/(2-p)$ when referring to the third inequality. **Norm-inequality conjectures.** The following statements are proposed as problems/conjectures:

(a) $\pi_{r,2}(i_{p2})\leq1$ for $p\in(1,2)$, with $r=2p/(2-p)$;

(b) $\|B\colon\ell_2\to\ell_p\|\geq\|B\|_{S_r}$ with $r=2p/(2-p)$;

(c) if $A$ is positive semi-definite, then $\|A\colon\ell_{p'}\to\ell_p\|\geq\|A\|_{S_r}$ with $r=p/(2-p)$ and $p'=p/(p-1)$.

These are presented as possible counterparts to the lemma used to obtain a sharp estimate on $\lambda'$ and are not resolved in the supplied text. They correspond to different proofs of the preceding norm lemma.
365405.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.15118

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
365405.source_name: Stanislaw Szarek and Pawel Wolff, “Radii of Euclidean sections of _p-balls”, arXiv:2410.15118 (2025).

365327.title: The parameter-boundary conjecture for the reverse Mittag–Leffler inequality
365327.statement:
Let $E_{\alpha,\beta}$ be the two-parameter Mittag–Leffler function. A **complete Bernstein function** is understood in the standard sense, and consider the global reverse inequality

$$
\left|E_{\alpha,\beta}(z)\right|\ge E_{\alpha,\beta}(\operatorname{Re}z)\qquad\text{for every }z\in\mathbb{C}.
$$

**The parameter-boundary conjecture.** There exists an increasing convex function $f:[2,\infty)\to[3,\infty)$ with $f(2)=3$ such that, for every $\alpha\ge2$,

$$
\left|E_{\alpha,\beta}(z)\right|\ge E_{\alpha,\beta}(\operatorname{Re}z)\ \text{globally}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\log E_{\alpha,\beta}\ \text{is a complete Bernstein function}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\beta\le f(\alpha).
$$

At $\alpha=2$ the corresponding boundary is known to be $f(2)=3$, and the paper gives partial support for extending this description to $\alpha>2$. The conjecture also predicts monotonicity and convexity of the boundary separating the parameter regions.
365327.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11852

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “The above figure illustrates our current findings and open questions, and concludes the paper.”
365327.source_name: Roberto Garrappa, Stefan Gerhold, Marina Popolizio and Thomas Simon, “On some inequalities for the two-parameter Mittag-Leffler function in the complex plane”, arXiv:2410.11852 (2025).
